item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
5B.9 is mixed, leaning negative. Tshisekedi’s 2024 macro team did show some competence: the IMF says reserves were built, inflation was easing, and corrective measures were taken after fiscal slippage tied to the eastern conflict. But the year still featured high inflation, weak budget credibility, slow reform, commodity and security shocks, and repeated blame-shifting rather than a consistently candid account of failures.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Democratic Republic of the Congo: 2024 Article IV Consultation, Sixth Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement** — IMF, 2024-07-15, https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/07/15/democratic-republic-of-the-congo-2024-article-iv-consultation-sixth-review-under-the-551892  
  - Claim: The IMF said the economy remained resilient, reserve accumulation continued, inflation was easing but still high, and the program mostly met targets. It also said the fiscal deficit overshot because of conflict-linked spending, and the authorities adopted corrective measures.  
  - IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`

- **Democratic Republic of the Congo: Selected Issues** — IMF, 2024-07-15, https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/07/15/democratic-republic-of-the-congo-selected-issues-551897  
  - Claim: Revenue mobilization improved, but remained low; tax capacity, especially around mining, still needed major reform. This supports some policy learning, but also shows the state had not solved structural fiscal weakness.  
  - IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.5`

- **Macro Poverty Outlook for Congo, Democratic Republic of: April 2024** — World Bank, 2024-04-03, https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099434404082425237  
  - Claim: The World Bank said terms-of-trade deterioration and higher imports were maintaining large current-account and fiscal deficits and pressuring the currency with pass-through to inflation. It judged growth and poverty reduction prospects favorable, but vulnerable to commodity and geopolitical shocks.  
  - IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.6`

- **Discours sur l’État de la nation 2024** — Présidence RDC, 2024-12-12, https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/discours_sur_letat_de_la_nation_2024_le_chef_de_l_etat_dresse_un_bilan_porteur_despoir  
  - Claim: Tshisekedi claimed reserves had reached about $6.12 billion and the exchange rate had stabilized, and said measures were being taken to protect purchasing power. This is favorable, but it is self-reported and should be weighted below IMF/World Bank evidence.  
  - IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`

- **Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts: report** — Reuters, 2024-01-15, https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/  
  - Claim: A civil-society report said CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. That is direct evidence of weak financial stewardship and low honesty in public administration.  
  - IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.5`

- **Army disarray hobbles Congo’s fight with Rwanda-backed rebels, officers say** — Reuters, 2024-07-17, https://theprint.in/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/2160048/  
  - Claim: Senior officers described mismanagement, poor logistics, demoralized troops, and over-reliance on proxies. Tshisekedi reportedly told Wazalendo to be brought in line, but the overall picture was one of weak crisis management rather than clean control.  
  - IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.6`, `5B.7`

- **Army disarray hobbles Congo’s fight with Rwanda-backed rebels, officers say** — Reuters, 2024-07-04, https://d2233.cms.socastsrm.com/2024/07/04/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/  
  - Claim: Tshisekedi threatened to declare war against Rwanda while the same report described dependence on proxy forces and weak discipline. This is evidence of escalatory rhetoric and limited candor about the state’s own weakness.  
  - IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.7`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a clean 2024 source giving ruler-level unemployment outcomes, debt dynamics, or a direct audit of whether crisis responses were consistently truthful. Most usable evidence is macro-level IMF/World Bank analysis plus a few Reuters or presidency readouts.
- There is also no strong direct evidence of a systematic “lessons learned” cycle beyond the IMF’s notes on corrective measures and the late-year reshuffle.
